title: CP2334-22 Recycling of District Council's Glass Bottles and Jars
description:
As a Waste Disposal Authority (WDA) DCC is responsible for the disposal of waste that the District Councils of Devon collect, known as Local Authority Collected Waste (LACW). DCC works in partnership with all 8 District Councils in Devon as well as the unitary authorities (UA) of Torbay. The partnership, known as DASWC (The Devon Authorities Strategic Waste Committee), consists of representatives at both officer and councillor level from all Devon District Councils and Torbay Council.\r
\r
From 1st April 2024, Waste Glass from Exeter City Council and the District Councils of East Devon, Mid-Devon, North Devon and Teignbridge will require collection and haulage from their respective Waste Collection Points for Recovery at the Contractor's Waste Recovery Point(s). The Waste Collection Point locations are listed within the specification provided in the contract documents, along with the estimated annual tonnage. Appendix A within the procurement documents provides further detail regarding each Waste Collection Point.\r
\r
The estimated value of this contract as stated within this contract notice is based off only the historic haulage costs payable to the winning contractor. However there are a number of additional elements to the value of the contract that are tied to the published letsrecycle.com rates, due to the variable nature of this value it is not possible to provide expected values for this element of the contract. Any prospective bidder should ensure they have fully read and understood all elements of the specification in order to accurately determine its value.\r
\r
The Contract will be for an initial period of three years with option to extend for a further two years

title: CP2300-22 - Contract for the Treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste
description:
Devon County Councils current contract arrangements for the transportation and treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste collected by the eight district councils within Devon is due to expire at the end of March 2024 and as such DCC are seeking to reprocure this service.  It is intended that the new contract will operate from 1st April 2024 for an initial period of five years with the option to extend the contract by a period or periods totalling a maximum further 5 years.\r
\r
Organic Sweepings Waste mainly consists of organic matter and as such DCC wishes the waste to be treated to allow it to be recycled e.g. into a compost like product or similar.\r
\r
The service requirement has been divided into two lots and DCC intends to let a contract for each lot.   Bidders can submit bids for one or both lots with no limit on the number of lots to be awarded to one provider.  Bids for each lot must be independent and not reliant on being awarded both lots.\r
\r
The Lots are as follows\r
\r
Service Lot 1 Contract for the transportation and Treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste from the District Councils of \r
East Devon\r
Exeter\r
Mid Devon\r
North Devon\r
South Hams\r
Torridge\r
West Devon\r
\r
Organic Sweepings waste arising from the District Councils covered in Lot 1 will require transportation from Waste Collection Points provided by DCC or District Council to the Contractors Waste Treatment Point for Treatment.\r
\r
During the 2022 23 Financial Year approximately 3600 tonnes of Organic Sweepings were collected as part of the District Councils covered by Lot 1 sweeping operations. \r
\r
Service Lot 2 Contract for the transportation and Treatment of Organic Sweepings Waste from Teignbridge District Council.\r
\r
The Contractor is required provide their own Waste Reception Point within the administrative boundary of Teignbridge District Council to which Organic Sweepings Waste can be delivered by Teignbridge District Council.   After Teignbridge District Council has delivered their Organic Sweepings Waste to the Contractors Waste Reception Point the Contractor shall transport the waste to the Contractors Waste Treatment Point for Treatment.\r
\r
During the 2022 23 Financial Year Teignbridge District Council collected approximately 950 tonnes of Organic Sweepings as part of their sweeping operations.\r
\r
cpvDescriptionExpanded: Sewage, refuse, cleaning and environmental services

title: CP2590-24 Devon,Plymouth and Torbay Energy Opportunities, Supply Chains and Infrastructure prospectus
description:
This is a standalone opportunity to develop an Energy Opportunities, Supply Chains and Infrastructure Prospectus aimed at both Government, Crown Estate and business. This should highlight energy opportunities, related supply chains, skills and infrastructure, focusing strongly on Floating Offshore Wind, hydrogen potential and ports. It should cover Devon, Torbay and Plymouth, linking strategically to any new Local Growth Plans, with a strong focus on the Northern Devon offer and where relevant the related Plymouth offer, including from the Plymouth and South Devon Freeport. This should include, if possible, an element of modeling and mapping of potential employment and skills quantums and also where possible link to the local defence sector.

The bidders should be able to produce documents in a format and style that aligns with Crown Estate and Government department needs, plus be attractive to businesses that wish to invest. An awareness of the need to pitch in a style to both people who need detail and to those who are limited in time is required.

The intention is for a final document to be produced by end March 2025, informed by and in close alignment with the release of the Government's Industrial Strategy, an emerging Devon and Torbay Local Growth Plan and where relevant, the emerging North Devon and Torridge Green Hydrogen Route Map

title: CEFAS24-112 Contract for services for outline water quality monitoring in the Taw and Torridge catchment in North Devon
description: Cefas requires water quality monitoring as part of a case study in the Taw and Torridge catchment in North Devon to deliver output 6.2. 'Report of findings benefits/barriers to using auto-sampling compared to spot sampling as a mean of assessing risks to coastal organisms'. To support this, Cefas requires the trialling of continuous water quality monitoring methods, using in-situ sondes and passive samplers, to inform catchment and hydrodynamic models of the Taw, and test their effectiveness in predicting the impacts on coastal health of, e.g., discharges arising from intense rainfall events, as well as their inter-operability with other data sources. These results will be compared with spot sampling methods and existing regulatory EA data.

title: Scaffolding Framework 2024
description:
Westward Housing Group (WHG) wish to appoint contractors to provide services across our stock portfolio. Contractors will be required to provide advice, quotations and scaffolding erection and removal to WHG properties as and when required. 

The tender is divided into five Lots by geographical area:

Lot 1	West Cornwall to Bodmin		(all TR postcodes)

Lot 2	Mid & East Cornwall and Plymouth	(all PL postcodes)

Lot 3	South Devon				(all TQ postcodes)

Lot 4	East Devon and Taunton		(EX1-17 & EX24)

Lot 5	North Devon				(EX18-23 & EX31-39)

 
You may bid for any number of lots.
You must be able to service the entire area of your chosen Lot(s).
In the pricing document is a tab for you to indicate which Lots you are applying for.


The Framework

title: CP2549-24: Devon and Somerset Standing List of Approved Contractors (SLoAC) 2025
description:
The Devon & Somerset Standing List of Approved Contractors (the SLoAC) provides a set of pre-qualified contractors for Maintenance, Improvement, and Building Works up to £2,000,000 per project, with most works ranging between £5,000 and £250,000, and for works below £5,000.\r
\r
SLoAC 2025 will replace the existing SLoAC, which has been in operation since 1st April, 2016, and will expire on 31 March, 2025. All interested contractors, including those currently on the existing list must re-apply to join SLoAC 2025. SLoAC 2025 is anticipated to commence April 2025, and will run for 4 years (Until 31st March 2029) with a break clause at the end of the second year (31 March 2027) and an option to extend for a further 4 years in 2 years increment (until 31 March 2033) at the Authority's discretion.\r
\r
The SLoAC will be re-opened periodically (anticipated to be annually) in order to enable contractors to apply to join the list. If in the Authority's reasonable opinion, specific work categories have sufficient numbers of contractors in a work category, the Authority reserves the right not to open those work categories to new applications to prevent having excessive numbers of contractors. In this initial application period no limit will be set to the number of contractors that will be accepted into a work category. The Authority also reserves the right to include additional works categories when the arrangement is reopened.\r
\r
Contractors will be appointed to the SLoAC based on achieving certain minimum standards through pass/fail questions. The award of specific projects will be subject to a competitive procurement process for each individual project. Only approved contractors on the SLoAC will get an opportunity to be selected to participate in a competitive processes when a needs arises. To be approved, contractors must obtain and maintain accreditation from our Comprehensive Accreditation Service Provider.. This is not a condition of joining the SLoAC but a condition for being selected to take part in a competitive process when a need arises.\r
\r
SLoAC is divided into 37 work categories, including 31 general and specialist categories,5 general agricultural categories, and a Principal Contractor category. Some of the most used work categories include Refurbishment and Repair, Heating, Roofing, Windows and Doors, New Build and Extension, and Agricultural Building - Build, Repair, and Maintenance. Contractors may apply for as many work categories as they wish to be active in.\r
\r
Devon has been subdivided into 8 geographical areas, plus the Torbay and Plymouth unitary authority areas, and Somerset into 5 geographical areas for the purpose of the SLoAC. Contractors may choose to operate in any number of these areas, subject to qualification.\r

title: CP2393-23 - Devon Domestic Abuse Integrated Support Service
description:
The service is for all who are experiencing domestic abuse, there are five delivery elements, each designed to integrate seamlessly to form one fully integrated service. Across the five elements, provider(s) will seamlessly transition between the elements and functions that enhance the victim/survivors' experiences.  \r
\r
Currently there are separate services under different contractual arrangements, these will be bought together into a single unified service. \r
\r
The service is for:\r
- Victims or survivors of Domestic Abuse and their children who require support in the community \r
- Victims and survivors of Domestic Abuse (over the age of 16) and their children residing in Devon who need to, are accessing or have recently accessed safe accommodation as a result of said abuse.  \r
- Those that perpetrate domestic abuse and cause harm who are willing to engage in restorative opportunities to address their behaviours \r
\r
Delivery elements in scope: \r
- Single Entry Gateway, Navigation Support and community engagement  \r
- Support in Domestic abuse Safe Accommodation and Refuge, Staying Put and resettlementâ€¯ \r
\r
Community support including:  \r
- Specialist victim support for moderate and high-risk DA \r
- Whole family support to non-violent parent and childrenâ€¯â€¯â€¯ \r
- Engagement with those that cause harm to elicit behaviour change \r
- Trauma responsive Recovery therapeutic Supportâ€¯â€¯ \r
- Support in safe accommodation for women experiencing multiple disadvantages including domestic abuse and sexual violence \r
\r
This integrated service will need to operate within a complex system and will proactively seek to collaborate, co-deliver, co-locate with other parts of the system including but not limited to, family hubs, (Safeguarding) Front Door and other parts of the system as opportunities emerge.    \r
\r
Bidders are invited to a launch event for this opportunity to familiarise bidders with the tender documentation and process on the 10 June 2024, 10.00am - 11.30am on Microsoft Teams. Interested bidders should email jolene.roberts@devon.gov.uk, this email address must only be used to arrange attendance at this event.  If you unable to attend this event, a recording will be made available on the tendering portal alongside any questions and answers.  Any questions in specific relation to the specification, we ask providers to submit these via the tendering portal.\r

title: Field-based surveys during the overwintering period to establish spatio-temporal distribution of oystercatchers across foraging habitats in the Taw-Torridge Estuary
description: This contract is for the delivery of field-based surveys during the overwintering period to establish spatio-temporal distribution of oystercatchers across foraging habitats in the Taw-Torridge Estuary. Two 8 hour surveys, each involving two ornithologists, will be conducted per month (over a spring tide and a neap tide) between October 2024 and February 2025 (inclusive) in the Taw-Torridge Estuary, North Devon.

title: Great South West High Value Manufacturing Research
description:
The Great South West (GSW) is looking to procure a suitably qualified party to deliver an evidence based review of the scale of High Value Manufacturing across the Great South West. Information of particular interest includes:\r
i.	Number of businesses and people employed within the industry\r
ii.	Amount of money it generates for the economy\r
iii.	Level of exports accounted for by manufacturing businesses\r
iv.	Scale of investment in R&D\r
v.	What the main manufacturing sectors are within the Great South West\r
vi.	Which sectors are forecast to see the greatest growth \r
Stakeholder engagement should form part of your approach, including:\r
•	Manufacturing groups: Plymouth Manufacturers Group, Cornwall Manufacturers Group, Dorset Engineering and Manufacturing Cluster and North Devon Manufacturers Association, together with SWMAS, the High Value Manufacturing Catapult and the South West Manufacturers Network.\r
•	Sector clusters: SW Defence & Security Cluster, Maritime UK SW, WEAF and Nuclear SW.\r
•	Partner organisations: Local Economic Partnerships. \r
The intention is to use this information to promote the Great South West's manufacturing strengths and target key interventions that will enable the forecast growth to be realised.
